about: Bowed low, with his joined hands resting on the altar, the priest asks God that the offering be carried by the hands of His holy Angel to the altar on high before the divine majesty. The prayer does not name the Angel. The clause beginning with “ut” leads to “repleámur”: those who receive the Body and Blood of Christ ask to be filled with every blessing and grace.

seg.nr: The priest bows low and lays his joined hands upon the altar.

seg.tr: We humbly ask You, almighty God: command that Your holy Angel carry these offerings in his hands to Your altar on high, before Your divine majesty:

a.g: command that these offerings be carried

seg.tr: so that all of us who
through this participation at the altar

seg.nr: The priest joins his hands and makes the sign of the cross once over the Host and once over the chalice.

seg.tr: receive the most holy Body and Blood of Your Son,

ex.w035: The form is future perfect, “will have received”. The same spelling could be the perfect subjunctive, “may have received”. The purpose clause settles the future perfect, which English prose gives as the present “receive”.

seg.tr: may be filled with every heavenly blessing and grace.
Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.
